newsitem.title: USA: U.S. wireless infrastructure expands - Dataquest.
newsitem.headline: U.S. wireless infrastructure expands - Dataquest.

text.p: The United States wireless infrastructure market grew by 63 percent, to $5.3 billion, in 1996, up from $3.3 billion the previous year, according to Dataquest, a market research and consulting company.

Dataquest said Wednesday the strong growth was from massive spending by telecommunications equipment companies in infrastructure for digital wireless telephone services, known as personal communications services or (PCS). The digital wireless is seen as the successor to the cellular telephone.
"Despite the health of the overall wireless infrastructure market, the cellular infrastructure market saw negative growth," it said.
Dataquest said PCS spending rose to $2.8 billion in 1996 from $530 million in 1995.
"Northern Telecom (Ltd ) gained the most in this buildout as it was the only company to win sizable contracts for CDMA and PCS-1900 technologies," it said.
Dataquest said Lucent Technologies Inc held its lead in the U.S. market in both cellular and PCS, but Northern Telecom showed the strongest growth with more than 100-percent growth.

Sweden's AB LM Ericsson and Motorola Inc posted steady cellular and PCS growth, but lost market share due to Northern Telecom's aggressiveness in winning PCS contracts. Ericsson and Motorola were nevertheless posied for global growth since each company had larger installed bases than Lucent and Northern Telecom internationally, it added.
Dataquest is a Gartner Group Company.
